```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Distribution fits a 90-day goal better. B's buyers self-discover tools in the Shopify App Store, a marketplace with merchant search built in. A depends on SEO, where Hyperping already ranks for the 'Statuspage is overpriced' angle, and on Product Hunt, which the brief itself says needs an existing audience to convert.",
    "B's proof that the model works is stronger. The brief cites a solo founder (Zigpoll) reaching $125K MRR in this exact category, with a link. A's best example, Instatus, is about $10k MRR, and the brief describes its growth as roughly $500/mo after years in market.",
    "B's price floor is less hostile. Its free incumbents cap usage (50, 100 or 200 responses or orders per month), which pushes growing stores onto paid tiers of $25–$149/mo. A's brief says a new entrant is 'effectively selling against $0' because OneUptime offers a free status page with unlimited manual monitors.",
    "B's demand evidence shows willingness to pay. The Reddit merchant already tried calling customers manually and gave up, which points toward paying for automation. A's pain quotes target Statuspage's prices, but cheap or free alternatives already address that pain.",
    "Both briefs describe saturated markets that a six-week build can scope. Neither has a clear edge on how hard the product is to build. The edge comes from distribution and from usage caps that force upgrades."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's main demand signal is a Reddit thread title asking why the market leader charges $399/month. It is a single title, not a buyer saying they would switch to a new paid vendor. A's own competitor list already answers that complaint with OneUptime's free tier, Hyperping at $29 and StillOnline at $9. So the quote shows dislike of incumbent pricing, not demand for another paid entrant.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe mature, crowded markets, and neither shows how a new entrant would get its first paying customer. B has real risks. Zigpoll took two years to gain traction. A zero-review app may struggle to earn merchant trust with order data. Shopify app review requirements and timeline are marked [unsourced], which could delay launch inside a 90-day window. B wins mainly on its marketplace channel and usage-capped free tiers, not on decisive evidence."
}
```
